previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and heart failure was admitted for evaluation of a nonhealing foot ulcer following a prior toe amputation. He underwent a right lower extremity angiogram to assess blood flow, which showed arterial blockages but sufficient perfusion for healing. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the admission. On postoperative day one, he developed hyperkalemia with a potassium rise from 5.5 to 6.5, prompting an urgent two-hour hemodialysis session with a low-potassium bath. His lisinopril was discontinued and amlodipine increased per nephrology guidance. He was discharged home on day two in stable condition with medication adjustments, wound care instructions, and follow-up arranged with vascular surgery.

radiology_notes.text:
AV FISTULA DUPLEX

Duplex evaluation was performed of right upper extremity surgical AV fistula. 
The loop graft is thrombosed.  The draining vein basilic and brachial arteries
are patent.

IMPRESSION:  Thrombosed right upper extremity loop graft.

To clarify for coding purposes:

Real time ultrasound guidance was used for both antegrade and retrograde
access. 
Images were saved to PACS.

INDICATION:  Thrombosed right upper extremity arteriovenous graft.  Evaluate
for occlusion and thrombectomy.
 
COMPARISON:  U/S ___.
 
OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, the attending radiologist, and Dr. ___,
the fellow.
 
MEDICATIONS:  Fentanyl (25 mcg).  tPA was administered via the AngioJet device
for a total of 10 mg.  4000 units of heparin was administered systemically. 
Local anesthesia was provided with approximately 10 cc of 1% lidocaine.
 
FLUOROSCOPY:  38.4 minutes, 158 mGy

CONTRAST: 110 mL Optiray

PROCEDURE:  
1. RUE AV graft fistulogram.
2. Balloon angioplasty of the right brachiocephalic vein stenosis. 
3. Chemical and mechanical thrombolysis of thrombosed graft.
4. ___ balloon sweep of the arterial inflow.
5. Balloon angioplasty of the intragraft stenosis.
 
DESCRIPTION:  After written informed consent was obtained, the patient was
brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The
left upper extremity was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure timeout and huddle was performed per the ___ protocol.
 
Clinical examination demonstrated a firm , palpable but non-pulsatile graft in
the right upper arm.  Further evaluation by ultrasound demonstrated a
completely thrombosed graft with patent arterial inflow and venous outflow. 
Using ultrasound and fluoroscopy, the inflow and outflow levels were
identified and the skin was marked with an indelible marker. 
 
Antegrade access into the thrombosed graft (directed towards the venous
outflow) was obtained using a micropuncture system .  The micropuncture wire
was exchanged for a Glidewire and the micropuncture sheath upsized to a ___ Fr
___ tip sheath. The Glidewire was advanced into the outflow vein and with
the assistance of a Kumpe catheter, multiple attempts were made to gain
central access, but were unsuccessful. Digital subtraction venogram
demonstrated complete occlusion of the bracheocepalic-SVC confluence.  Using
the venogram for guidance, a Glidewire was eventually advanced across the
stenosis into IVC. The wire was then exchanged for a ___ wire with the
assistance of the Kumpe catheter. 

We then turned our attention to the retrograde access and used ultrasound
guidance and a micropuncture access system to advance a glide wire through
soft clot within the graft.  A 6 sheath was then advanced over the glide wire.
Care was taken not to advance the wire into the inflow artery prior to
chemical thrombolysis. At this time, balloon angioplasty of the central
stenosis was performed with a 6 mm balloon.

The AngioJet device was placed in thrombectomy mode and mechanical
thrombectomy was performed from the antegrade and retrograde approach and
repeated twice. Next, tPA was administered using the AngioJet pulse spray
device in the anterograde direction for a total of 6 mg beginning at the
proximal aspect of the stent.  Further tPA was administered for a total of 4
mg in a retrograde fashion from the arterial anastomosis back into the mid
graft.  The tPA was allowed to dwell for approximately 10 minutes. Mechanical
thrombectomy was repeated.  Balloon maceration was performed throughout the
graft using a 6 mm balloon.  The antegrade sheath was then connected to a side
arm heparinized saline flush. 
 
Next, our attention was turned to the arterial inflow.  A ___ balloon
pull-back sweep was performed to the tip of the retrograde sheath using a
___ embolectomy balloon. This resulted in improved flow and a faint thrill
in the graft. A Kumpe catheter was advanced over the glide wire allowing a
full angiographic run outlining the entire graft and the central veins
demonstrating residual outflow vein and central venous stenosis. Repeat
angioplasty of the central stenosis was performed with an 8 mm and 10 mm
balloon, sequentially. 
 
Repeat fistulagram demonstrated significant improvement with moderate residual
stenosis.  The sheaths were then removed and hemostasis was achieved with
pursestring sutures.  There was no immediate complications. A satisfactory
thrill was noted in the graft at the termination of the procedure.

The patient was transferred to dialysis.
 
FINDINGS:

1.  RUE graft thrombosis. Restoration of flow in the  graft following
mechanical and pharmacologic thrombectomy.

2.  Complete chronic occlusion of the left brachiocephalic vein with multiple
collaterals. Moderate residual stenosis following sequential balloon
angioplasty up to 10 mm.

IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Thrombectomy of right forearm AV graft using an AngioJet device and 10 mg
of TPA.
 
2.  ___ embolectomy of the arterial anastomosis.
 
3.  Balloon angioplasty of the brachiocephalic vein to 10 mm.
 
4.  Angioplasty of intragraft stenosis to 6 mm.
  
5.  Satisfactory restoration of flow was achieved with a palpable thrill on
examination. The patient should return for elective repeat balloon angioplasty
of the central stenosis in ___ weeks. This lesion may require stenting if it
re occludes in the short term.
